claims.text: Born in England in 1957, Dane felt called to the Lord's work young and sought to join the Jesuits in 1980.
In 1982 Dane destroyed a neonate in Washington, D.C., and in that moment was flooded with names, faces and scenes, sure of a calling to hunt vampires.
Varga came from Hungary in early adulthood, speaking no English, and never came to accept the new country after being treated as stupid and lazy for it.
Learned and drawn to the occult, Varga sought out a hidden circle of spiritualists and mediums in Detroit.
Jean Lisle is of the Samedi, a slave in what is now Haiti when given the name Jean; the birth name is lost.
A rotting monster forced its blood on Lisle in the Embrace, and every night since has been spent on revenge for slavery, a bloodlust that never fades.
Juggler, a Brujah, has told no living vampire of the Embrace or the sire, and tells childer that the Old World life does not matter.
The one clue to Juggler's origin is a slide into Italian when angry; otherwise Juggler speaks unaccented American English.
DiMatto, child of a Giovanni cousin, was Embraced in 1980 after a youthful fascination with the darker side of the family.
A violent amateur film made at sixteen impressed the family and set DiMatto on a path into filmmaking.
Modius, a Toreador Embraced in middle age, says little of the past simply because no one has asked in years.

Modius claims a hand in founding the Arcanum and to have been its first supernatural patron, and to have known every literary or occult figure of the 19th and early 20th centuries; Modius may believe it.
